title: Callaway chart editor grid (13x5) with column adjustments and 0.5 worst-hole increments

requirements.summary: Replace the Admin Callaway chart editor’s row-based table with a fixed 13x5 gross-score editing grid for both 18-hole and 9-hole charts.
acceptanceCriteria: In the Admin Panel > Callaway Chart Editor, the chart editing surface is a 13 (rows) x 5 (columns) grid for gross-score chart editing.
The previous row-based table UI (Row / Lower Bound / Upper Bound / Worst Holes / Adjustment) is no longer the primary editing format for gross scores.
The grid is rendered for both 18-hole and 9-hole tabs (even if their underlying defaults differ).

file_operations.description: Refactor the chart editing UI to render a fixed 13x5 grid of gross-score cells (for both 18-hole and 9-hole tabs), replacing the current variable-length row table as the primary editor. Use existing shadcn-ui components (e.g., Tabs, Input, Label, Card, Button, Alert) to compose the grid and section headers; verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Introduce/adjust chart data utilities so the app can represent and consume the new fixed 13x5 grid chart shape for gross-score mapping (for both 9- and 18-hole modes), while still supporting read-only display and calculation lookups.

Update the chart display section to render correctly with the new underlying chart representation (grid-derived values), ensuring the leaderboard view can still show the active chart without relying on the legacy row-list structure. Use existing shadcn-ui Table/Card components; verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

requirements.summary: Add per-column Adjustment inputs (one per grid column) and persist/load them with the edited chart, including reset-to-default support.
acceptanceCriteria: Each of the 5 columns has a clearly labeled Adjustment input that is visually associated with that column (one adjustment value per column).
Changing a column’s adjustment affects the calculated adjustment used for any gross score that maps to that column.
Saving and reloading the chart preserves the per-column adjustments.
Reset-to-defaults restores the default per-column adjustments.

file_operations.description: Add an Adjustment input row (or header controls) for each of the 5 columns and wire these values into the editor state so they apply to all gross-score cells in the same column. Use existing shadcn-ui Input/Label and layout utilities to keep each adjustment visually associated with its column; verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Extend localStorage persistence to save/load the new chart representation including the 5 per-column adjustment values, and ensure reset-to-defaults restores default column adjustments along with default grid contents.

Update chart lookup helpers so the effective adjustment for a gross score is computed as the per-column adjustment associated with the mapped column (and used consistently by calculation and display).
Update Callaway calculation to use the new chart lookup output, ensuring the adjustment applied for a player is derived from the correct column adjustment for their gross score mapping.

requirements.summary: Support worst-holes values in 0.5 increments in the editor and calculation, and ensure all result displays remain stable with fractional deductions.
acceptanceCriteria: The worst-holes input(s) in the chart editor accept values like 3, 3.5, 4, 4.5 (step 0.5) and reject values not on a 0.5 increment.
Chart validation allows non-negative worst-holes values in 0.5 increments.
Callaway deduction calculation correctly handles X.5 worst holes by deducting the sum of the worst X holes plus half of the next-worst hole (based on sorted worst hole scores).
All screens that display calculation results (leaderboard and breakdown) continue to work with fractional worst-hole deductions without crashing or showing NaN.
Backend Callaway calculation (backend/main.mo) is updated to match the same half-hole deduction behavior if backend results are used for ranking/output.

file_operations.description: Change worst-holes editing inputs in the new grid to accept 0.5 steps (e.g., number input with step 0.5) and add UI-level validation feedback for values not aligned to 0.5 increments. Use existing shadcn-ui Input/Alert components; verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.
Update chart validation logic to allow non-negative worst-holes values in 0.5 increments (and reject values not on a 0.5 boundary) for the persisted chart format.
Update deduction logic to correctly handle fractional worst holes: for X.5, deduct sum of worst floor(X) holes plus half of the next-worst hole score, preventing NaN and ensuring numeric stability.
Adjust types used in UI result data (e.g., deduction and worstHolesUsed) as needed to safely represent fractional worst-hole usage/deductions without breaking rendering or ranking logic.

Ensure leaderboard rendering formats fractional deduction/adjustment values safely (no NaN), and continues to rank by net score correctly when decimals are possible. Use existing shadcn-ui Table components; verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Ensure the breakdown panel displays fractional worst-holes usage and deductions consistently and safely in the calculation explanation line. Use existing shadcn-ui Card/Badge components; verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

requirements.summary: Make localStorage chart loading backward compatible with legacy row-based saved charts by migrating or safely falling back to defaults.
acceptanceCriteria: If old edited chart data exists in localStorage (saved by the previous row-based format), the app does not crash on Admin screen load.
The persistence layer either (a) migrates old stored data into the new 13x5 + per-column adjustments representation, or (b) safely ignores invalid/legacy data and falls back to defaults.
Save and Reset actions continue to work after the change.

file_operations.description: Implement backward-compatible loading for legacy localStorage data (previous row-based array format) by detecting legacy shapes and either migrating them into the new 13x5 grid + per-column adjustments representation or clearing them and falling back to defaults, ensuring Admin load never crashes.

Update editor initialization and Save/Reset flows to use the updated persistence API and to handle migrated/fallback data paths cleanly, preserving existing Save and Reset behaviors. Use existing shadcn-ui Button/Alert components; verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Add/adjust helpers needed for migration (e.g., mapping from legacy row-based ranges to the new fixed gross-score grid values and deriving per-column adjustments), keeping runtime lookups robust even when legacy data is encountered.
